history_summary.value: A breed defined by its curled plumage, from a frizzle gene believed to have arisen in Asia and reported there since the eighteenth century. Selective breeding for exhibition turned it into a distinct breed recognised in nine European countries and Australia, though in the United States frizzled birds are judged as a feather type within their own breed rather than as a separate breed.
